req-pm-codec-contracts-1.text: A processor MUST decode every codec it lists exactly as its contract and its normative vectors define it, except for a parameter value or coding feature it refuses with Unsupported feature under case (d) of Codecs; a vector's expected output or expected error category is normative.

req-pm-codec-contracts-2.text: When the description is loaded, a processor MUST check every encoding step against the contract of its codec: a parameter name the contract does not declare, a missing required parameter, and a literal value of the wrong type or outside the declared values are a Description error, and a value the contract defines but the processor does not implement is Unsupported feature (Codecs, case (d)).

req-pm-codec-contracts-3.text: A processor MUST raise a Description error, when the description is loaded, for a pipeline in which a step reads bytes where the step decoded before it produces samples, or samples where it produces bytes, or in which the first step decoded reads samples.

req-pm-codec-contracts-4.text: Every codec MUST honour the decoded-byte limit (Resource Limits) and cancellation, and MUST NOT allocate output beyond what remains of the limit before it has validated the sizes its input declares.

req-pm-codec-contracts-5.text: An HDL compiler SHOULD warn when a description names a catalogue-only concept in @encoded-with, a pipeline step or a candidate, since the description it compiles can be read but never decoded; it MUST still compile it, because recording the encoding of data no processor yet decodes is what the catalogue is for.

req-pm-codec-contracts-6.text: A codec raises it only where its contract declares it, and a processor MUST report it as a Description error, which no lenient mode continues past, never as a Validation error: the bytes are not at fault, the description is.

req-pm-codec-selection-1.text: The candidates of a step MUST name distinct codecs, and a processor MUST check each of them when the description is loaded as it checks a step that names its codec, raising Unsupported feature for a candidate whose codec it does not decode even when no input ever selects it.

req-pm-codec-selection-2.text: A String value that names none of the candidates, a shared local name included, MUST be raised as a Validation error; a value that is not a String is a Type / HEL error.

req-pm-codec-selection-3.text: A processor MUST raise a Description error, when the description is loaded, for a selecting step that carries a hexplain:codecParameter of its own, a step that carries both hexplain:codec and hexplain:codecFromExpression, and a selecting step without hexplain:codecCandidates or whose candidate list is empty.

req-pm-codec-sessions-1.text: A processor MUST NOT let a session outlive the parse that created it, and under bddo:PerInstance MUST NOT share one between two instances of the struct.

req-pm-conformance-1.text: It MUST implement every rule of this document that the classes it claims require, and it MUST NOT silently mis-parse a description that uses a construct outside them (see Conformance Classes).
req-pm-conformance-1.context: A conforming processor implements one or more of the conformance classes below, and states which.

req-pm-conformance-classes-1.text: abnd:nestedProfile is optional in this version: a Bundle Processor that does not assemble nested profiles MUST reject a bundle profile that uses one with Unsupported feature.

req-pm-conformance-classes-2.text: Its output MUST be a description that a Physical Parser (and, when the source declares mappings, a Semantic Emitter) processes exactly as it would the equivalent hand-written RDF.
req-pm-conformance-classes-2.context: The HDL language as specified there.

req-pm-conformance-classes-3.text: A refusal SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded rather than when the construct is first met in a stream.

req-pm-conformance-classes-4.text: A processor MUST NOT ignore a construct and parse on as though it were absent: a partly understood description yields a plausible but wrong tree, which is worse than no tree.

req-pm-conformance-classes-5.text: A processor MUST state which classes and which optional features it claims, the codecs it decodes (Codecs beyond the minimum set) and the further text encodings it decodes (Further encodings).

req-pm-conformance-classes-6.text: Tree documents and grouped key/value headers are no class's requirement: a processor that claims them MUST implement them exactly as Delimited, key/value and tree containers specifies, and one that does not MUST reject a description that uses them, when the description is loaded, and MUST NOT read such a container's fields by byte offset or as a flat header.

req-pm-conformance-classes-7.text: A Physical Parser MUST accept a description that declares a chunked layout and parse the field's bytes.

req-pm-conformance-classes-8.text: A processor that does not claim chunked-layout cell access MUST raise Unsupported feature when a cell is addressed through the chunk table and MUST NOT address the bytes as contiguous cells; one that does not claim other chunk orders MUST reject a dlv:chunkOrder other than dlv:rowMajor or dlv:columnMajor when the description is loaded.

req-pm-conformance-classes-9.text: It MUST be raised no later than the first time the construct would affect the result.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-1.text: A constraint whose conf:scope is a bddo:Struct MUST be evaluated once for every parsed instance of that struct, after the instance is complete, with instance and self bound to the instance, parent to the struct that holds it and root to the root of the input.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-2.text: A constraint whose scope is a bddo:Field MUST be evaluated once for every parsed value of that field — each element of a repeated field is one value, and an absent optional field fires nothing — with instance bound to the containing struct and self to the value.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-3.text: The input's format version is supplied by the caller; an evaluator MUST NOT guess it from the data.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-4.text: When no version is supplied, every requirement is evaluated and the report MUST state that version scoping was not applied.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-5.text: An evaluator MUST enforce resource limits on a run (at least the parse limits, and a limit on the number of findings).

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-6.text: When one is reached it MUST either fail with a ResourceLimit error or stop and return a report marked truncated, stating the limit; it MUST NOT return an unmarked partial report.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-7.text: A report written as RDF MUST be one conf:Run with exactly one conf:verdict (conf:Conformant or conf:NonConformant), exactly one conf:truncated flag, a conf:truncationReason when it is truncated, conf:versionScopingApplied (with the supplied version as conf:fileVersion when it is true), conf:failOn when the fail-on severity is not sh:Violation, one conf:outcome per requirement, and a conf:finding link to every finding; it names what was evaluated with conf:profile, conf:ruleSet and conf:input where it can.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-8.text: The report MUST validate on its own against the conf and req shapes: it MUST carry a copy of every req:Requirement, conf:Constraint and conf:ParseAttribution description it references, with each constraint's conf:scope typed bddo:Struct or bddo:Field, so that a finding's severity and attribution can be checked against its constraint and attribution without the profile.

req-pm-context-1.text: Fields already parsed within the current and ancestor nodes are visible; forward references (to fields not yet parsed) MUST raise an error, except where this document defers an evaluation until its references are bound: a struct-level size (Struct-level size), a conditional byte order (Byte order and bit order), and the expressions of Semantic Triple Emission that are evaluated over the complete tree — hexplain:valueExpression, the hexplain:condition of a hexplain:MappingRule (a map guard) and of a hexplain:ClassMappingRule (a means-when guard) — for which a field parsed later is simply a field.

req-pm-context-2.text: The alias is deprecated in HEL 1.0: a processor SHOULD warn when it loads a description that uses it, new descriptions MUST NOT use it, and an HDL compiler never emits it.

req-pm-context-3.text: An argument that is a literal, or a negated numeric literal, of the wrong kind for a typed parameter is known from the description alone: a processor MUST raise it as a description error, when the description is loaded.

req-pm-context-4.text: Any other argument is known only once it is evaluated: a processor MUST raise a value of the wrong type, a struct or an array as a Type / HEL error when the argument is evaluated (ParseField, Value), not as a description error.

req-pm-data-layouts-1.text: Before any cell is addressed, a processor MUST resolve the layout against the field's containing struct: each dlv:dimensionSizeFromField, dlv:dimensionStrideFromField, dlv:chunkSizeFromField and dlv:cellBitWidthFromField reads the named field (looked up as for bddo:sizeFromField), each dlv:dimensionSizeFromExpression, dlv:dimensionStrideFromExpression, dlv:chunkSizeFromExpression and dlv:cellBitWidthFromExpression is evaluated with the containing struct as instance (HEL, name binding), and the first holding arm of dlv:hasConditionalCellDataType and of dlv:hasConditionalDimensionOrder is selected (DLV conditional layout).

req-pm-data-layouts-2.text: A processor MUST resolve a computed form when the layout is resolved, before any cell is addressed, and never per cell, so that an expression that reads the stream position or a field of the struct yields one value for the whole layout.

req-pm-value-mapping-1.text: A Semantic Emitter MUST emit a mapped field that declares bddo:fixedPointScale k, itself or through its data type, as the number the integer stands for, the integer read times 2^k, in an xsd:decimal literal, which holds every such value exactly: the Q16.16 field holding 00 01 80 00 is emitted "1.5"^^xsd:decimal, and a scale of 2 on the integer 3 is emitted "12"^^xsd:decimal.

req-pm-value-mapping-2.text: A Semantic Emitter MUST support every scale from −4096 to 4096, so that a description whose scales stay within that range is portable.

req-pm-value-mapping-3.text: A processor MUST raise a description error for a bddo:fixedPointScale outside the range it supports, when the description is loaded or, at the latest, when the field is emitted; it MUST NOT emit an approximation of the scaled value or the integer unscaled.

req-hel-coercion-1.text: Arithmetic / bitwise operands MUST be numeric.
req-hel-coercion-1.context: These rules are normative and resolve the comparisons used throughout Hexplain (e.g. comparing a 4-byte ChunkType to 'IHDR'):

req-hel-coercion-2.text: Integer comparisons MUST be exact; mixed comparisons compare the exact represented numeric values without first rounding the Integer to Float.

req-hel-conformance-2.text: Parse all valid expressions per the ABNF grammar, and reject as a syntax error every string it does not generate, including out-of-range literals and unknown escapes.

req-hel-conformance-3.text: A processor that does not parse multi-part assets MAY leave asset and partExtension unimplemented, but MUST then raise a runtime error on an expression that uses them rather than resolving them to Null.

req-hel-conformance-4.text: Implement all operators and every core function with the specified precedence, the numeric semantics, and the value-type and coercion rules; and implement each extension group it claims in full.

req-hel-conformance-5.text: Reject, at load time, a description that calls a function of an extension group it does not implement, with an unsupported-feature error.

req-hel-conformance-6.text: Yield a Boolean in a boolean context, an Integer in a numeric context and a String in a string context, as the name-binding table gives for each property (e.g. a hexplain:valueExpression whose hexplain:valueDatatype is xsd:string yields a String); any other result is an error, and a Float is never an Integer, even one whose value is integral: a size expression that yields 2.0 is an error, not a size of 2.

req-hel-conformance-7.text: Report a runtime error (rather than silently continue) on type errors, integer overflow, shift counts out of range, out-of-range unsigned values, division/modulo by zero, out-of-range subscripts, undefined names and forward references.

req-hel-conformance-8.text: Accept, by default, expressions whose expression tree is at least 512 levels deep and at least 64 KiB long, when they are parsed and when they are evaluated, and quantifier and match-cost budgets of at least the Processing Model’s minimums; let the user configure all four limits; and report an expression beyond its configured nesting or length limit, a quantifier that exceeds its evaluation budget, a regular-expression match that exceeds its cost limit, and a deadline or cancellation as the Processing Model's ResourceLimit error, not as a syntax or runtime error: it is fatal in every mode, including a lenient one that records other errors and continues (Security and Privacy Considerations).

req-hel-conformance-9.text: Produce, for every row of hel-vectors.tsv whose functions it implements, the value the row gives — of the type the row states, where its expectation is typed (int:3, float:2) — or an error of the condition the row names; a row's message column is informative.

req-hel-conformance-10.text: An evaluator MUST count depth this way, so that a long flat sum or conjunction, which descriptions generate, is accepted whatever its length allows.

req-hel-core-functions-1.text: A conforming evaluator MUST implement every core function.
req-hel-core-functions-1.context: A literal whose value is too large to be finite in binary64 (1e999) is a syntax error, not Infinity; one too small to be distinguished from zero denotes zero.

req-hel-core-functions-2.text: Every argument MUST already be a String (or Bytes): there is no implicit conversion, so a number must be rendered deliberately rather than picking up whatever spelling the engine happens to use for it.

req-hel-core-functions-3.text: Integer or Float: the numeric value of string, whose lexical form MUST match NumericText below exactly.

req-hel-core-functions-4.text: The accessor MUST be exactly asset.<Part>, naming a part (e.g. partExtension(asset.Raster)); it is a runtime error otherwise, when the part is missing or more than one file was matched to it, and — like asset itself — when the description is not being parsed as part of an asset.

req-hel-error-conditions-1.text: A conforming evaluator MUST be able to state, for every error it raises, which of these conditions it is; it MAY report them under names of its own and with any message.

req-hel-expression-literals-1.text: A processor MUST accept an expression in a literal of either datatype and MUST evaluate the two alike: the datatype never changes what an expression means.

req-hel-expression-literals-2.text: Authoring tools SHOULD type the expressions they write bddo:HelExpression; an expression typed xsd:string remains valid.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-1.text: The first argument MUST be an array node.
req-hel-ext-quantifiers-1.context: Boolean: true when predicate holds for at least one element; false for an empty array.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-2.text: Each evaluation MUST yield a Boolean, else it is an error.
req-hel-ext-quantifiers-2.context: When the element is a struct node, param.n and a name that reaches a local binding MUST resolve against the element’s struct: param.n is the argument the element was parsed with, a bare name or instance.name may name a local binding of the element’s struct, and the parameters and bindings of the struct holding the expression are not reachable in the predicate.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-3.text: When the element is a struct node, param.n and a name that reaches a local binding MUST resolve against the element’s struct: param.n is the argument the element was parsed with, a bare name or instance.name may name a local binding of the element’s struct, and the parameters and bindings of the struct holding the expression are not reachable in the predicate.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-4.text: An evaluator MUST bound the total number of predicate evaluations during one evaluation of an expression, nested quantifiers included, by its configured quantifier limit (the Processing Model’s quantifier evaluations, at least 1,000,000 by default), and MUST report exceeding it as a ResourceLimit error.

req-hel-ext-temporal-1.text: The text MUST supply a full date and time.
req-hel-ext-temporal-1.context: datetime(string, pattern) | The pattern letters are yyyy (year), MM (month), dd (day), HH (hour 00–23), mm (minute) and ss (second); any other ASCII letter outside quotes is a malformed pattern; other characters match themselves, and text inside single quotes is literal.

req-hel-ext-temporal-2.text: Resolution is strict: every field MUST be in range for the date it names, so 30 February, day 00, month 13 or hour 24 is not a valid date-time and is never rolled over into another date.

req-hel-ext-temporal-3.text: It is a parameter supplied to the run: an evaluator MUST take it from the run and MUST NOT read it from the wall clock, so that re-running the same evidence gives identical results.
req-hel-ext-temporal-3.context: Integer: the reference instant of the run, in seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC.

req-hel-ext-text-1.context: matches(string, pattern) | Boolean: whether the whole of string matches the regular expression pattern (the match is anchored at both ends: matches('IHDR', 'IH') is false).

req-hel-ext-text-2.text: Profiles SHOULD confine patterns to the constructs common to the major regular-expression dialects — literal characters, ., bracket classes with ranges and negation, * + ? {m,n}, |, grouping with ( ), and the escapes \d \s \w — whose meaning is the same everywhere; the meaning of other constructs is implementation-defined.

req-hel-ext-text-3.text: An evaluator MUST bound the cost of each match by its configured match-cost limit (the Processing Model’s regular-expression match cost, at least 2,000,000 by default), and MUST report a match that exceeds it as a ResourceLimit error, never as false and never as a Type / HEL error (Security and Privacy Considerations).

req-hel-ext-text-4.text: An evaluator MUST give every HEL-RE construct exactly that meaning, and MUST raise an argument error for a pattern that is not a HEL-RE expression: a construct of another dialect that XSD does not define — a back-reference (\1), look-around ((?=…)), a non-capturing or named group ((?:…)), an inline flag ((?i)), a lazy or possessive quantifier (*?, *+), \b, \B, \A, \z, a hexadecimal or octal escape (\x41, \101), an unknown escape — and an unescaped ^ or $ outside a character class, which XSD would read as literal characters and every other dialect as anchors (a pattern is anchored already; a literal ^ is written \^ and a literal $ as [$]).

req-hel-ext-text-5.text: A block escape names a Unicode block by Is and the block's name (\p{IsBasicLatin}): an evaluator MUST raise an argument error for a \p{Is…} or \P{Is…} whose block name it does not know, and for an unknown category, and MUST NOT read an unknown block as matching nothing or everything.

req-hel-ext-text-6.text: An unescaped - in a character class is a literal hyphen only as the class's first member (after a negating ^) or its last (before the closing ] or a subtraction's -[); anywhere else it MUST form a range between the single characters on either side of it, and a - that does neither ([a-c-e], a range whose end is below its start) is an argument error.

req-hel-ext-text-7.text: The characters that \p{…}, \P{…}, \w, \W, \d and the block names denote are those of one version of the Unicode Standard, the version of the implementation's platform: a processor that implements this group MUST state that Unicode version, for example 15.0, in its claims statement or in the environment of its implementation report (member unicode), so that two reports that disagree on a pattern over a recently assigned character can be told apart by it.

req-hel-ext-text-8.text: An implementation MAY bound the size and nesting of a pattern it compiles; a pattern that is a HEL-RE expression but too large or too deeply nested for the evaluator to compile MUST be reported as a ResourceLimit error, never as an argument error, which would say the pattern is not HEL-RE, and never as false.

req-hel-ext-text-9.text: A processor MUST bound the cost of a match including the iterations that consume no input: every iteration of a quantified group that the matcher performs counts toward the limit, whether or not it examines a character of the subject, so that a group able to match the empty string ((){20000}, (a?)*) cannot buy unbounded work from an empty subject; an evaluator that proves such iterations idle and does not perform them owes nothing for them.

req-hel-ext-text-10.text: A processor MUST NOT refuse a pattern on account of its counted quantifiers when it is within both figures: other bounds on a pattern — its length, its nesting — remain the implementation's own (above), and neither figure changes which patterns are HEL-RE, a bound up to 2^31−1 being well formed.

req-hel-extension-groups-1.text: A processor that does not implement a group MUST reject a description whose expressions call a function of that group when the description is loaded, with an unsupported-feature error naming the function and the group's IRI; it MUST NOT defer the failure to the first evaluation, where it would depend on the data.

req-hel-formal-grammar-1.text: HEL and HDL string literals share one escape set: \\ (backslash), \' (apostrophe), \" (quotation mark), \n (U+000A), \t (U+0009), \r (U+000D), \0 (U+0000), \xHH (the code point U+0000–U+00FF given by exactly two hex digits) and \uHHHH (the UTF-16 code unit given by exactly four hex digits; a high surrogate MUST be followed by a \uHHHH low surrogate, the pair denoting one code point, and a lone surrogate is an error).

req-hel-formal-grammar-2.text: An IntegerLiteral or HexLiteral denotes a non-negative Integer and MUST NOT exceed 2^63−1 (9223372036854775807, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF); a larger literal is a syntax error, not a wrap-around.

req-hel-formal-grammar-3.text: A FunctionName MUST NOT be a ReservedWord: an evaluator MUST read not(x), not (x) and not x alike, as the not operator applied to x (so not(a) and b is (not a) and b, by precedence), and instance(1), and(), true() are syntax errors, not calls.

req-hel-formal-grammar-4.text: An evaluator MUST report a syntax error for a root written as a function name (asset(1), param()) and for a root written as a key after a dot (x.param, x.asset, x.stream, x.self, x.root, x.instance): a Step is parent or a Name, and a Name is never a reserved word.

req-hel-key-resolution-1.text: Within one struct, field local names MUST be unique.
req-hel-key-resolution-1.context: Identifiers are not IRIs and are never expanded through @prefix declarations or a JSON-LD context: ChunkType means "the field named ChunkType in this struct", whatever namespace its IRI is in.

req-hel-key-resolution-2.text: A key MUST name a field declared by the bddo:Struct of the node it is applied to, or be the keyword parent; a bare name, or a key applied directly to instance, MAY also name a bddo:LocalBinding of that struct, and a key after param names a parameter.

req-hel-key-resolution-3.text: A name that is also a reserved word (instance parent root self stream asset param and or not true false) cannot be written as a bare name or a key, so a field, parameter or local binding that expressions need to reference MUST NOT have such a local name.

req-hel-key-resolution-4.text: The index expression MUST evaluate to a non-negative Integer strictly less than the array's length (elements are 0-based); otherwise a range error is raised.

req-hel-key-resolution-5.text: A processor MUST reject a description in which two fields of one struct share a local name, with a Description error when the description is loaded: an expression could not tell which of them a name reads.

req-hel-math-1.text: An Integer argument MUST be returned unchanged; a Float argument MUST be rounded exactly, on its binary64 value, and the result MUST be an Integer, so that ceil(n / 2.0) is a size.

req-hel-math-2.text: Arguments MUST be compared exactly, as the comparison rules compare an Integer with a Float, and the result MUST be the selected argument with its own type (min(2, 2.5) is the Integer 2, max(2, 2.5) the Float 2.5); when two arguments are equal the first of them is selected (min(1, 1.0) is the Integer 1, min(-0.0, 0.0) is -0.0).

req-hel-math-3.text: An Integer MUST be rendered as its decimal digits with a leading - when negative and no +, grouping or leading zeros (toString(-42) is '-42'); a Float MUST be rendered by the Float rendering below (toString(2.0) is '2.0', toString(0.1 + 0.2) is '0.30000000000000004', toString(1.0E7) is '1.0E7').

req-hel-math-4.text: With d those digits and e the decimal exponent such that the value is 0.d × 10^e, an evaluator MUST write a value whose magnitude is at least 10^−3 and below 10^7 in positional notation — the digits with the point after the e-th, zeros supplied on either side as needed, and at least one digit on each side of the point (123.0, 0.001, 1234567.0) — and every other value in scientific notation: the first digit, a point, the remaining digits or a single 0, then E and the exponent e−1 in decimal with a - when negative and no + (1.0E7, 1.5E-5, 1.7976931348623157E308, 4.9E-324), with a leading - for a negative value.

req-hel-math-5.text: They are functions of a number's value, not Integer arithmetic: an evaluator MUST accept an unsigned 64-bit Integer above 2^63−1 (Unsigned 64-bit values) as an argument of floor, ceil, trunc, round, abs, min, max and toString, and MUST NOT raise the out-of-range error that arithmetic on such a value raises.
req-hel-math-5.context: They take Integers and Floats only; a Null, Boolean, String, Bytes or node argument is a type error, and an argument count outside what is shown is a syntax error.

req-hel-math-6.text: The rendering is defined by the two rules above and by nothing else: no platform's number formatting is its definition, and an evaluator whose platform function differs on any value (several wrote more digits than the shortest before they were corrected) MUST NOT use it.

req-hel-name-binding-1.text: The table below is normative and complete: these are the HEL-bearing properties, and for each, what the roots instance, parent, root and self are bound to and what type the result MUST have.

req-hel-name-binding-2.text: New descriptions MUST NOT use it; a processor SHOULD warn when it loads a description that does; an HDL compiler never emits it.

req-hel-name-binding-3.text: For these three, and only these, the whole tree of the part is bound: a field declared later than the one carrying the expression MUST read as its parsed value, not raise a forward-reference error, and an absent optional field reads as Null (Processing Model, evaluation time).

req-hel-numeric-semantics-1.text: Integer-only +, -, *, / and unary - are exact within [−2^63, 2^63−1]; a result outside that range MUST raise an error, never wrap.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-2.text: Division and modulo by zero MUST raise an error, for Float operands as well as Integer ones: 1.0 / 0.0 is an error, not Infinity.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-3.text: The shift count MUST be an Integer in [0, 63]; a count outside that range MUST raise an error (it is not reduced modulo 64). >> is an arithmetic (sign-propagating) right shift.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-4.text: x << n MUST raise an error when x × 2^n is outside the signed 64-bit range, so 1 << 63 is an error.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-5.text: A parsed unsigned integer above 2^63−1 (from a uint64 field) keeps its exact value for comparisons and for Float arithmetic, but its use in Integer arithmetic, bitwise operations, shifts or indexes MUST raise an out-of-range error.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-6.text: Indexes MUST be non-negative Integers within the addressed collection; a Float, negative or out-of-range index MUST raise an error.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-7.text: Float % MUST be the truncated remainder of IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic (C's fmod, Java's and Kotlin's % on doubles), never the floored or the IEEE remainder operation: for finite operands the result is x - y * trunc(x / y) computed exactly, so it has the dividend's sign and a magnitude below |y| (5.5 % 2.0 = 1.5, -5.5 % 2.0 = -1.5, 5.5 % -2.0 = 1.5, -5.5 % -2.0 = -1.5, 6.0 % 2.0 = 0.0, -6.0 % 2.0 = -0.0); a finite dividend with an infinite divisor is returned unchanged (3.0 % (1e308 * 10.0) = 3.0), an infinite dividend or a NaN operand yields NaN, and a zero divisor is a division-by-zero error (above).

req-hel-operator-precedence-1.text: A guard MUST therefore be written with the ternary rather than with and: count(Items) > 0 ? Items[0] == 1 : false, not count(Items) > 0 and Items[0] == 1.

req-hel-operator-precedence-2.text: The ternary evaluates its condition (which must yield a Boolean) and then only the selected branch; both branches SHOULD have compatible types, and the result takes the type of the selected branch.

req-hel-operator-precedence-3.text: The operands of and, or and not MUST be Booleans, and both operands of and and or are type-checked: false and 1 is an error even though false decides the result.

req-hel-operator-precedence-4.text: The logical and and or operators MUST evaluate BOTH operands: they do not short-circuit, so an expression whose right operand raises — a division by zero, an out-of-range subscript — raises even when the left operand already decides the result.

req-hel-reserved-roots-1.text: The key after the part name MUST name a field of that part's root struct.

req-hel-reserved-roots-2.text: A processor MUST raise a Description error, when the description is loaded, for param.n in an expression whose instance struct declares no parameter n, and for param without a key: whether a struct has a parameter is known from the description alone, so this is never deferred to the data.

req-hel-reserved-roots-3.text: Inside the predicate of all/any over struct elements instance is the element, so a processor MUST make that check against the element’s struct, not the struct holding the expression, wherever the description determines the element’s struct (the collection is a path of fields whose declared types are structs, none chosen at parse time); where it does not, a param.n the element’s struct lacks is an undefined name when it is evaluated.

req-hel-reserved-roots-4.text: An evaluator MUST resolve a .parent step that follows a key step or a subscript from the path, as the struct instance that holds the field that step names, whatever the type of the value the step read (a scalar field has a holder as a struct field does), and MUST NOT report it as a key applied to a scalar.

req-hel-reserved-roots-5.text: The stream, a parameter scope and the asset are not struct instances, so a key step taken on stream, param or asset records no holder: an evaluator MUST read stream.length.parent, param.n.parent and asset.Header.parent as Null, as it reads stream.parent, and MUST NOT report them as a key applied to a scalar or resolve them to the current struct.

req-hel-versioning-1.text: A later 1.x version MAY add functions and extension groups, but MUST NOT change the value or the error an expression that is valid under HEL 1.0 produces.

req-hel-versioning-2.text: The function library is divided into a core set, which every conforming evaluator MUST implement, and named extension groups, which an evaluator MAY implement.

req-hel-versioning-3.text: A processor MUST read the declared HEL version when the description is loaded, and MUST raise a Description error for a bddo:helVersion that is not of that form.

req-hel-versioning-4.text: A declared major version other than 1 MUST be refused with an Unsupported feature error when the description is loaded: HEL 1 rules cannot be assumed to read it.

req-hel-versioning-5.text: A call to a function name that is neither a core function nor in an extension group of the version the evaluator implements MUST be rejected when the description is loaded, as an Unsupported feature error when the declared version is a later 1.x version than the evaluator implements (the name may be one that version defines), and as a Type / HEL error otherwise (the name is simply not HEL).

req-hdl-checksums-1.text: In crc(…) a compiler MUST accept the six parameters width, poly, init, refin, refout and xorout in any order, each exactly once, and MUST report an ERROR for a missing, repeated or unknown parameter, a width outside 8..64, a poly, init or xorout that is negative or not below 2^width, and a reflection flag that is not true or false.

req-hdl-checksums-2.text: A CRC's width, named or custom, MUST equal the bit width of its checksum field's integer type; any other checksum field is an ERROR (the Processing Model makes it a description error).

req-hdl-clauses-1.text: An integer @fixed on a numeric field is emitted typed with the field's XSD type (@fixed 9994 on an i32 becomes "9994"^^xsd:int) and is compared by value; a hex @fixed stays xsd:hexBinary and, on a numeric field, MUST have exactly the field's width in bytes (Processing Model, Fixed value).

req-hdl-clauses-2.text: A field MUST NOT carry two clauses of one kind, and a compiler MUST report an ERROR for a second size (two […]), count (two repeat), offset (two @at), fixed value (two @fixed), byte order (two @endian) or type selection (two of switch and dispatch), rather than emit both values of a property the Processing Model reads once.

req-hdl-clauses-3.text: It MUST also report an ERROR for a derive field with a repeat clause (a derived field reads no bytes, so it has no elements), for any two of @pipeline, @codec switch and @encoded-with on one field, and for two declarations of one struct, header, table or document name in a document.
req-hdl-clauses-3.context: A field MUST NOT carry two clauses of one kind, and a compiler MUST report an ERROR for a second size (two […]), count (two repeat), offset (two @at), fixed value (two @fixed), byte order (two @endian) or type selection (two of switch and dispatch), rather than emit both values of a property the Processing Model reads once.

req-hdl-clauses-4.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a literal outside the range of its position — a field size or struct @size below 1 (bytes[0], bytes[-3]), a repeat count or offset below 0 (repeat -2, @at -2), a stride below 1 (stride 0) — and for a FLOAT literal in any of these positions (bytes[2.0], repeat 1.5, @at 1e0): they take integers, and an integral float is not one.

req-hdl-clauses-5.text: The literal positions differ in what they accept, and a compiler MUST hold each to its own set. @prop takes an IRIREF, a CURIE, or an INT, HEX, STRING, true or false literal, never a bare NAME (write the string "x" or the CURIE ex:x).

req-hdl-clauses-6.text: A compiler MUST emit the field's own bddo:bitOrder for a field-level @bit-order and MUST NOT fold it into the struct's or into the neighbouring fields', since two adjacent bit fields with different orders are read under their own orders (a change of order starts a new byte).

req-hdl-clauses-7.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a literal outside the range of its position — a field size or struct @size below 1 (bytes[0], bytes[-3]), a repeat count below 0 (repeat -2), an offset below 0 from any base but current (@at -2, @at -2 from stream-end), a stride below 1 (stride 0) — and for a FLOAT literal in any of these positions (bytes[2.0], repeat 1.5, @at 1e0): they take integers, and an integral float is not one.

req-hdl-clauses-8.text: A negative literal offset from current is in range, because the Processing Model lets an offset from the cursor move backward (Negative offsets): a compiler MUST accept @at -2 from current and MUST emit it in the expression form, bddo:atOffsetFromExpression "-2" beside bddo:offsetBase bddo:currentPosition, never as a bddo:atOffset, whose value is not negative.

req-hdl-compilation-model-1.text: Errors at any stage are reported as diagnostics with a source location; a conforming compiler MUST NOT raise an uncaught exception to its caller on malformed input, and MUST report at least one ERROR diagnostic for input it cannot faithfully compile.

req-hdl-conformance-section-2.text: Accept both the text and YAML surfaces and parse each into the same abstract model, such that a text document and its YAML mirror compile to isomorphic RDF graphs, modules, imports, keyed dispatch and seek scope included (§YAML Surface).

req-hdl-conformance-section-3.text: Accept every text-surface document generated by the grammar (subject to the static rules stated alongside it) and report an ERROR diagnostic for any text-surface input it does not generate.

req-hdl-conformance-section-4.text: Mint IRIs per §IRI Minting and bind prefixes per §Prefixes; a CURIE whose prefix is not bound MUST yield an ERROR diagnostic, never a warning and never a silently emitted IRI.

req-hdl-conformance-section-5.text: Apply the field-form-vs-expression-form rule and resolve expression identifiers per §Expressions and the HEL name-binding rules, emitting canonical HEL validated against [[?hel]]; a bare reference to an undeclared name MUST yield an ERROR diagnostic, and so MUST every other static error §Expressions lists, a forward reference included, wherever it is statically determinable (§Expressions): the compiler knows the declaration order of every struct it compiles, so every bare-name forward reference, and every root.

req-hdl-conformance-section-6.text: Emit BDDO/Core/DLV/hx-bundle triples whose meaning matches the mappings in this document, such that the output satisfies the SHACL shapes of the targeted vocabularies for any well-formed input.

req-hdl-conformance-section-7.text: Report malformed input as source-located diagnostics and never raise an uncaught exception to its caller; input that cannot be faithfully compiled MUST yield at least one ERROR diagnostic.

req-hdl-conformance-section-8.text: Preserve raw-turtle bodies verbatim in the output graph.

req-hdl-conformance-section-9.text: Report an ERROR for a field name or alias that is not an ASCII HEL identifier or is reserved (asset included; §Lexical Structure), and for every layout name that does not name a sibling (§Expressions).

req-hdl-conformance-section-10.text: By default, confine import resolution to an import root (the root document's directory unless the caller names another) and reject, with an ERROR, any import whose real path lies outside it (Import resolution). A compiler MAY offer an explicit unrestricted mode for trusted callers.

req-hdl-conformance-section-11.text: Report an ERROR diagnostic for a language version declaration naming a version it does not implement.

req-hdl-expressions-1.text: A conforming compiler MUST validate every synthesized expression against the HEL grammar and MUST report an ERROR diagnostic, at compile time, for: a bare identifier that does not resolve to a declared field; a forward reference, including a field's reference to itself outside @valid; self outside repeat until, @valid and a quantifier predicate; a stream.

req-hdl-expressions-2.text: The names in a layout — a dimension's size and chunk, cell-bits from, chunks offsets/lengths, a stride expression, and the guards of cell switch and order switch — are sibling references like any other: each MUST name a field of the containing struct, and an unknown one is an ERROR.

req-hdl-expressions-3.text: A root.k path whose k is not a field of the root struct is an undeclared name, except when some struct of the document declares @root-key: k may then be a key only the data names (Processing Model, Root key), and a compiler MUST then accept root.k for any identifier k.

req-hdl-expressions-4.text: A compiler MUST resolve the names of a repeat until condition as follows.
req-hdl-expressions-4.context: Introduces: Over struct elements a bare name in a repeat until condition is looked up first among the element's fields, emitted as instance.x, and, failing that, among the fields of the struct that contains the repeated field, emitted as parent.x (HEL binds parent to that struct there). A name both declare is an ERROR, since either reading would be a guess; a container field declared after the repeated field is a forward reference. Over scalar elements a bare name is a field of the containing struct, as in every other field-level expression.

req-hdl-expressions-5.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a key step applied to a field that holds a scalar (n.foo), or to a repeated field without a subscript (es.size; the number of elements is len(es)): neither has fields.

req-hdl-form-rule-1.text: For any size, offset, or count clause: when the expression is exactly one sibling field name, a conforming compiler MUST emit the specific …FromField object property; otherwise it MUST emit the …FromExpression datatype property carrying the synthesized HEL string.

req-hdl-form-rule-2.text: A compiler MUST emit every integer it writes as an xsd:integer literal (Turtle's bare integer), except where this document names another datatype: a size, repeat count, offset, alignment, radix, bit length, skip count, dimension size, stride, chunk extent, cell width, part count, enumeration raw value, dispatch key, pipeline parameter or @prop value is an xsd:integer, never an xsd:long or xsd:int, whatever range the targeted property declares; an integer @fixed on a numeric field takes the field's XSD type (Fixed values).

req-hdl-grammar-1.text: It defines the complete text surface of HDL: a conforming compiler MUST accept every document the grammar generates (subject to the static rules below and elsewhere in this document) and MUST report an ERROR diagnostic for any document it does not generate.

req-hdl-grammar-document-1.text: A format document MUST declare at least one struct or container unless it declares a bundle or asset; the struct marked @root, else the first struct, is the root.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-1.text: Every Expr, Guard and CoverExpr denotes a HEL expression: after the rewriting of §Expressions, its text MUST match the Expression production of the HEL grammar.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-2.text: Backtick (` … `): the text is raw HEL, emitted verbatim with no rewriting at all, so it MUST already be valid HEL (single-quoted strings, no 0b literals, explicit instance.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-3.text: Backticks are all or nothing: a BACKTICK_EXPR MUST be the whole Expr or Guard; one inside a longer run is an ERROR.

req-hdl-grammar-fields-1.text: A PipelineStep MUST NOT name a parameter twice; a value that is a CodecLiteral (a Literal other than a NAME, or an IRIREF), a FLOAT or a CodecList is a hexplain:parameterValue, and any other value is an Expr emitted as hexplain:parameterExpression (§Semantic Mapping).

req-hdl-grammar-keywords-1.text: instance parent root self stream asset param and or not true false — HEL reads them as roots, operators or literals, so a compiler MUST reject a field, alias, parameter or let binding so named.

req-hdl-grammar-layout-1.text: Every NAME in a layout (sizes, chunk extents, cell-bits from, offsets, lengths, stride expressions, guards) is a sibling reference and MUST name a field of the containing struct.

req-hdl-grammar-lexical-1.text: A NAME used as a field name or alias MUST additionally be a HEL identifier (§Lexical Structure).

req-hdl-iri-minting-1.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR when two declarations of one document mint the same IRI, whatever kinds they are — at the later of two declarations of one kind, and at either of two of different kinds: two structs, two top-level enums, two dispatch tables, two bundles or two assets of one name; two parameters of one struct of one name, or a parameter and a field or local binding of its struct; a struct, a top-level enum, a dispatch table, a bundle, an asset, an asset's part and a top-level field that share a name with one another (struct Grid and bundle Grid; asset roads with a part Grid); an as alias that spells any of these or another alias; and two arms of one table whose keys mint one IRI (the string keys "a b" and "a%20b", both <base>T.arm.a%20b.str).

req-hdl-iri-minting-2.text: A compiler MUST NOT resolve the collision by renaming, by dropping one declaration or by merging the two.

req-hdl-layout-1.text: This example reads values from another part of a multi-file asset (asset.Header.…) and the grid part's own extension (partExtension(asset.Grid); a part is named by the struct its part spec is described-by), so it can only be processed by a processor in the Bundle Processor conformance class (Processing Model §Conformance classes); a Physical Parser handed the raster part alone MUST fail the asset references with an error rather than read them as Null.
req-hdl-layout-1.context: These are two independent conditionals over one set of dimensions rather than one conditional layout, which would multiply into a case per (interleave, width) pair.

req-hdl-lexical-1.text: Although the lexer folds - and ., a field's name and its as alias, a struct parameter's name and a let binding's name MUST be HEL identifiers — an ASCII letter or _ followed by ASCII letters, digits and _, and not one of instance parent root self stream asset param and or not true false — because expressions reach a field by that name (asset is HEL's multi-part root, so a field so named could never be read).

req-hdl-lexical-2.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a hyphenated, dotted or reserved field name (the reference compiler suggests byte_order for byte-order).

req-hdl-lexical-3.text: Digits are ASCII only: a compiler MUST report a lexical ERROR for a non-ASCII digit (the Arabic-Indic ٣, the fullwidth １) outside a string, comment or raw-turtle block, never read it as a digit.

req-hdl-modules-1.text: An import path is resolved relative to the directory of the file that contains it, and MUST resolve within an import root.

req-hdl-modules-2.text: escape, or a symbolic link pointing out of the tree, since links are resolved to their real path before the check — MUST be rejected with an ERROR diagnostic on the import line; the root is inherited by every nested import, so an imported module cannot widen it.

req-hdl-modules-3.text: A compiler MUST bound the bytes it reads through imports, both per imported file and in total for one compilation, and MUST report an imported file that would exceed either bound as an ERROR diagnostic on the import line (or imports: entry), without compiling it: an import graph is input the compiler did not write, and an unbounded one lets a document make it read without limit.

req-hdl-modules-4.text: A compiler MUST emit each arm as an IRI, <ns#Table.arm.key> in the namespace of the document that declares the arm (an integer key as its decimal digits and nothing else; a string key percent-encoded as a quoted key is, §IRI Minting, followed by the suffix .str — every string key carries the suffix and no integer key does, so that 7 and "7" are T.arm.7 and T.arm.7.str, "ftyp" is T.arm.ftyp.str, and no string key, "7.str" included, can spell another key's IRI; an imported table's alias:Table written alias.Table), never as a blank node, so an arm an extend dispatch contributes from another module has a name of its own.

req-hdl-modules-5.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR, on the import line (or imports: entry) that brings in the later of them, when two different documents of one compilation have the same base namespace, whether it was declared with @namespace or derived from the format or module name: <ns>Box would then be whatever both documents declare under that name, merged, and no check within either document can see it.

req-hdl-parameters-1.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for: a type position that supplies a number of arguments other than its struct's number of parameters (including arguments for a struct without parameters, and none for one with parameters); a parameterised struct in a position that cannot state arguments — a dispatch default, a layout cell type, a described-by part struct, and the root struct (@root, or the first struct) — since none of them has a caller that could supply them; two parameters, two bindings, or a parameter, binding and field of one struct, that share a name; a parameter type other than the five words above; param used as a name, and param.x in a struct with no parameter x; a forward or self reference in an argument, which is evaluated at the position of the field that passes it, or in a let expression, which is evaluated at the binding's position; a clause on a let (it has a name and an expression, nothing else); a let binding named where a field is required — a layout extent or stride, a checksum range bound, @root-key, @lang-from — since it has neither bytes nor a place in the tree; a let in a header, table or document, whose members have no evaluation order; and parameters on a header, table or document (in YAML, params beside a kind other than struct), which has no scope to bind them in.

req-hdl-parameters-2.text: Where instance is an element — the condition of a repeat until over struct elements, and the predicate of all/any over them — a compiler MUST resolve a bare name against the element struct’s parameters and let bindings (param.name, instance.name) and check param.x against the element struct’s parameters, not those of the struct holding the field, and MUST report an ERROR for a name that is only a parameter of the holding struct, which param never reaches there; the holding struct passes such a value to the element struct as an argument instead.

req-hdl-prefixes-1.text: In particular, aspect and register prefixes (araster, acolor, ageom, menc, and the part-role register's own conventional prefix rpr, which is bound to the same namespace as role) are not predeclared: a description that uses one MUST bind it with use.

req-hdl-prefixes-2.text: A CURIE whose prefix is none of the above — not predeclared, not bound by use, and not an import alias — is an error: a conforming compiler MUST report an ERROR diagnostic for it wherever it occurs (a means, @datatype, @encoded-with, @pipeline step, @object, @unit, @prop, enum symbol, register, part role, carries, or type position), and MUST NOT emit the unexpanded CURIE as an IRI.

req-hdl-semantic-1.text: A catalogue-only concept, one that carries no hexplain:codecContract (Processing Model, codec status), has no contract at all, so no processor decodes it; a compiler SHOULD report a WARNING diagnostic, not an ERROR, for @encoded-with, a pipeline step or a switch arm that names a catalogue-only concept, and MUST still compile the description.

req-hdl-semantic-2.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a name in the media-encoding register's namespace that is no concept of the register (menc:Zlip), in any of those positions: a misspelt codec is not a codec nobody decodes yet, and compiled with a warning it would be a description that can never be read.

req-hdl-types-1.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a bracket size after a fixed-width numeric type (u8 … f64be) or a variable-length integer type: the Processing Model ignores a size on a fixed-width field, so u32[4] could only mislead its reader into expecting four bytes of something else, or four elements.

req-hdl-versioning-1.text: A compiler that does not recognise the declaration, or that recognises it but does not implement the version named, MUST report an ERROR diagnostic (unsupported language version) and MUST NOT compile the document under the rules of a different version.

req-hdl-yaml-1.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST restrict implicit boolean resolution to true/false; the YAML 1.1 words on/off/yes/no are strings (so a struct field or switch key named on is not silently coerced).

req-hdl-yaml-2.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST report an ERROR for a mapping that repeats a key (YAML leaves the outcome to the loader, and last-wins would drop a field or a clause silently) and for a null entry in a sequence (a stray - in a field list), rather than skip it.

req-hdl-yaml-3.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST read a quoted scalar in a literal position as a string even when it spells a hex literal, and MUST read the mapping { hex: "0x…" } as the hex byte string its value spells, wherever a HEX literal is accepted.

req-hdl-yaml-4.text: A compiler SHOULD report a WARNING for a quoted scalar that spells a hex literal in a literal position, since the bytes were almost certainly meant.

req-hdl-yaml-5.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST report an ERROR for a quoted "0x…" in one of these positions, since they take bytes and it is a string (any quoted scalar is an ERROR for sync and terminator; a quoted delimiter that does not begin 0x is the UTF-8 bytes of its text).

req-hdl-yaml-6.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a key that the table does not list for the mapping it appears in, in every mapping of the document: the top level, a struct, an enum, a field, and every mapping nested in them that the table names — a type, a switch, a dispatch, a checksum and its crc, a layout, an entry of dims, chunks, a pipeline step, a bundle, a part, an asset.

req-hdl-yaml-7.text: A compiler MUST likewise report an ERROR for a listed key whose value is not of the kind the key takes — a mapping or a sequence where a scalar is required (name: { a: 1 }, size: [4]), a scalar where a sequence or a mapping is required (fields: 3, layout: u8), a sequence where a mapping is required (structs: [ … ]) — and MUST NOT coerce the value, skip the key or read it as absent.

req-ce-conf-conformance-1.text: A processor that evaluates profiles is a Conformance Evaluator, and MUST follow Processing Model §Conformance Evaluation.

req-ce-conf-conformance-2.text: A constraint whose conf:scope is a bddo:Struct MUST be evaluated once per parsed instance, with instance and self bound to it; one whose scope is a bddo:Field MUST be evaluated once per parsed value of the field, with instance bound to the containing struct and self to the value.

req-ce-conf-conformance-3.text: A false assertion MUST yield exactly one conf:Violation finding at the constraint's conf:severity, citing every requirement the constraint cites; any other result, or an evaluation failure, MUST yield one conf:RuleError finding.

req-ce-conf-conformance-4.text: A finding MUST NOT cite a requirement its constraint does not cite.

req-ce-conf-conformance-5.text: A parse error MUST be reported as a conf:Parse finding with its conf:errorCategory (a conf:ErrorCategory; Dispatch is a category of its own), attributed to the requirement of the profile's conf:ParseAttribution for that category, or to no requirement when none names it.

req-ce-conf-conformance-6.text: conf:message placeholders MUST be interpolated as that property defines: {field} is the focus node's path, and {value} the evaluated value when it is unambiguous, left as written otherwise.

req-ce-conf-conformance-7.text: Version scoping MUST use only a version the caller supplies, compared with req:appliesToVersion by exact string equality.

req-ce-conf-conformance-8.text: Without one, every requirement MUST be evaluated and the report MUST say that version scoping was not applied.

req-ce-conf-conformance-9.text: A run stopped by a resource limit MUST either fail with a ResourceLimit error or be reported as truncated; requirements it did not reach MUST receive conf:NotReached.

req-ce-conf-conformance-10.text: Every requirement of the profile MUST receive exactly one outcome, with the precedence conf:NotApplicable > conf:Errored > conf:Evaluated > conf:NotReached > conf:NotExercised; a requirement no constraint cites is conf:NotExercised.

req-ce-conf-conformance-11.text: A report written as RDF MUST state its conf:verdict and conf:truncated flag once each and link every finding with conf:finding.

req-ce-conf-conformance-12.text: It MUST validate on its own against conf/shapes.ttl and req/shapes.ttl, carrying copies of the requirements, constraints and parse attributions it references; a blank-node requirement is copied under a skolem IRI.

req-ce-req-conformance-1.text: It MUST carry exactly one non-empty req:requirementId, req:fromStandard and req:statement, and exactly one req:discrepancyType.
req-ce-req-conformance-1.context: A requirement is identified by its IRI.

req-ce-req-conformance-2.text: Within one graph, two distinct requirements MUST NOT carry the same (req:fromStandard, req:requirementId) pair after surrounding whitespace is removed from both values and req:fromStandard is compared ignoring case; req:RequirementIdentityShape enforces it.

req-ce-req-conformance-3.text: req:appliesToVersion values are compared by exact string equality with the input's format version, which the caller of a conformance run supplies; an evaluator MUST NOT infer it (Processing Model §Conformance Evaluation).

req-ce-req-conformance-4.text: req:discrepancyType classifies a defect and MUST NOT be used to set a finding's severity; severity is the citing constraint's conf:severity.

req-bddo-addressing-1.text: Before parsing the field, the processor MUST advance the cursor to the next multiple of this value (padding bytes are skipped).

req-bddo-bitfields-1.text: A run of bit fields SHOULD align to a byte boundary; a processor MUST pad to the next byte before parsing a subsequent non-bit field.

req-bddo-checksum-algorithms-1.text: A bddo:CustomCrc MUST state each of the six exactly once: a width from 8 to 64, a polynomial (in normal, unreflected form, without its top term), an initial value and a final XOR that are non-negative integers below 2^width, and the two reflection flags as xsd:boolean literals.

req-bddo-conformance-1.text: A validator checking a BDDO description graph against § Normative SHACL Shapes MUST either include the BDDO rdfs:subClassOf axioms of § Normative OWL Vocabulary in the graph it validates, or apply RDFS subclass closure to that graph before validating.

req-bddo-core-datatypes-1.text: All conforming processors MUST support these types.
req-bddo-core-datatypes-1.context: BDDO provides a normative set of built-in primitive data types.

req-bddo-core-datatypes-2.text: A field of one of these types MUST NOT declare a width or terminator — bddo:size, bddo:sizeFromField, bddo:sizeFromExpression, bddo:sizeToEndOfStream, bddo:terminator or bddo:bitLength — because its length comes from the data and a declared one could contradict it.

req-bddo-core-datatypes-3.text: A processor MUST read a bddo:uint24 as the unsigned value of its three bytes in the effective byte order (0 to 16,777,215), and a bddo:int24 as the same 24 bits read as a two's-complement integer (−8,388,608 to 8,388,607): FF FF FE big-endian is −2, never 16,777,214.

req-bddo-core-datatypes-4.text: It MUST read a bddo:float16 as an IEEE 754 binary16 value — one sign bit, five exponent bits with bias 15, ten fraction bits — including subnormals (exponent field 0: the fraction times 2^−24), both zeros, both infinities and NaN, and its value is the exact binary16 value as a HEL Float, with no rounding, since every binary16 value is exactly a binary64 one: 3C 00 is 1.0, 00 01 is 2^−24, 7B FF is 65504, 7C 00 is +Infinity.
req-bddo-core-datatypes-4.context: A processor MUST read a bddo:uint24 as the unsigned value of its three bytes in the effective byte order (0 to 16,777,215), and a bddo:int24 as the same 24 bits read as a two's-complement integer (−8,388,608 to 8,388,607): FF FF FE big-endian is −2, never 16,777,214.

req-bddo-data-type-rule-1.text: Value MUST be one of bddo:baseInteger, bddo:baseFloat, bddo:baseString, or bddo:baseBytes.

req-bddo-field-properties-1.text: Value MUST be a bddo:DataType or a bddo:Struct.
req-bddo-field-properties-1.context: bddo:dataType | The Field's default data type.

req-bddo-field-properties-2.text: A Field MUST have either a bddo:dataType or a bddo:hasConditionalDataType (or both).

req-bddo-field-properties-3.text: Keys MUST be unique per table across all contributing graphs.

req-bddo-field-properties-4.text: A Field MUST use at most one sizing mechanism, and variable-length types (bddo:bytes, bddo:string) MUST use exactly one sizing or termination mechanism — except for a field of a bddo:DelimitedRecords, which is exempt because its extent is set by its container's delimiters.

req-bddo-field-properties-5.text: Value MUST be an xsd:hexBinary literal.
req-bddo-field-properties-5.context: bddo:terminator | A byte sequence terminating a variable-length field.

req-bddo-field-properties-6.text: Value MUST be one of the encoding individuals (bddo:utf8, bddo:ascii, bddo:utf16le, bddo:utf16be, bddo:latin1).

req-bddo-field-properties-7.text: A Field MUST use at most one repetition mechanism.
req-bddo-field-properties-7.context: bddo:repeatCount / bddo:repeatCountFromField / bddo:repeatCountFromExpression / bddo:repeatUntil | Turn the field into an array parsed a fixed number of times, a number read from another field, a number computed by a HEL expression, or repeatedly until a HEL boolean expression evaluates to true.

req-bddo-field-properties-8.text: A HEL boolean expression that MUST hold once this field is parsed; if it evaluates to false the parse fails with a validation error.

req-bddo-field-properties-9.text: Each value MUST be an xsd:hexBinary literal.
req-bddo-field-properties-9.context: On a bddo:DelimitedRecords (see Delimited Text Records): the byte sequence splitting the byte run into records, splitting a record into values, and (in a bddo:KeyValueHeader) splitting a key from its value.

req-bddo-field-properties-10.context: bddo:quoteChar / bddo:escapeChar | On a bddo:DelimitedRecords: the byte that quotes a value so it may contain a delimiter, and the byte that escapes the following byte.

req-bddo-parameterised-structs-1.text: Every place that names a parameterised struct as a type MUST supply exactly one argument per parameter, and a place that names a struct without parameters, or a bddo:DataType, MUST supply none; bddo:ArgumentArityShape checks the three direct forms.

req-bddo-parameterised-structs-2.text: Within one struct, a parameter MUST NOT share its name with a field, a local binding or another parameter of that struct.

req-bddo-parameterised-structs-3.text: A local binding MUST be named by an IRI, MUST NOT share its name with a field, a parameter or another binding of its struct, and MUST NOT be a member of a text container (a delimited, key/value or tree container), whose members have no evaluation order; bddo:LocalBindingShape checks the first and the last.

req-bddo-parameterised-structs-4.text: A text container — a bddo:DelimitedTable, bddo:DelimitedRecords, bddo:KeyValueHeader or bddo:TreeDocument — MUST NOT declare bddo:hasParameter: its members are located by key, column or path rather than read in order, so it has no scope to bind arguments in, and a processor raises a Description error for it (Processing Model, Errors).

req-bddo-structural-properties-1.text: The object MUST be an rdf:List whose members are bddo:Field or bddo:LocalBinding resources, to preserve order.

req-bddo-structural-properties-2.text: Value MUST be bddo:BigEndian or bddo:LittleEndian.
req-bddo-structural-properties-2.context: bddo:endianness | The byte order for a bddo:Struct, bddo:Field, or bddo:DataType.

req-bddo-structural-properties-3.text: Value MUST be bddo:MSBFirst or bddo:LSBFirst.
req-bddo-structural-properties-3.context: bddo:bitOrder | The bit-packing order for bit-level fields in a Struct.

req-bddo-structural-properties-4.text: A byte sequence a processor MUST scan for before parsing this bddo:Struct.

req-bddo-structural-properties-5.text: Value MUST be an xsd:hexBinary literal.
req-bddo-structural-properties-5.context: bddo:syncOnMarker | A byte sequence a processor MUST scan for before parsing this bddo:Struct.

req-bddo-structural-properties-6.text: Bounds the Struct's total byte extent, establishing a bounded region for its children: descendant reads MUST NOT cross it, bddo:sizeToEndOfStream resolves to the region end, and trailing/padding bytes are skipped.

req-dlv-conditional-1.text: Both are first match wins, so a more specific arm MUST precede a more general one: a .flt arm has to come before a NBITS 32 arm, because a float grid is also 32 bits wide and the width arm would otherwise claim it.
req-dlv-conditional-1.context: The same rule applies as above: no matching arm leaves the order undetermined, and an unevaluable condition does not fall through to the next arm.

req-dlv-properties-1.context: dlv:cellDataType | The data type of each cell.

req-dlv-properties-2.context: dlv:dimensionSize / dlv:dimensionSizeFromField | The length of a dlv:Dimension: a fixed xsd:positiveInteger, or read from a bddo:Field.

req-core-punning-1.text: A DL reasoner may therefore reject or ignore parts of these modules; that is not a defect of a description, and processors MUST NOT rely on DL entailments.

req-core-static-mapping-properties-1.text: The subject MUST be a bddo:Struct and the object MUST be an owl:Class.

req-core-static-mapping-properties-2.text: The subject MUST be a bddo:Field and the object MUST be an rdf:Property.

req-core-static-mapping-properties-3.text: A processor MUST decode the block; when the field's data type is a bddo:Struct, it MUST re-parse the decoded bytes against it as a bounded sub-stream.

req-geometry-document-1.text: A measure ordinate MUST NOT be treated as elevation or time without an explicit semantic mapping.

req-geometry-document-2.text: Legacy dimensionality values alone cannot distinguish XYZ from XYM; importers SHOULD emit both flags when the source carries them.

req-raster-document-1.text: Described bands MUST NOT exceed a declared band count; omission of some bands is allowed in a partial RDF projection.

req-raster-document-2.text: SampleArray dimensions MUST be a complete, finite ordered RDF list.

req-raster-document-3.text: Logical array order MUST NOT be treated as a byte-stride or chunk-order declaration.

req-raster-document-4.text: Calibration values MUST be finite; NaN MAY be a no-data sentinel and requires NaN-aware detection.

req-raster-document-5.text: Temporal, vertical, spectral, ensemble and other scientific axes MUST NOT be forced into fixed X/Y/Z categories.

req-spatialref-document-1.text: A GeoTransform MUST carry four finite coefficients (originX, originY, scaleX, scaleY) and MAY omit a skew, which is then zero (north-up); a skew that is present MUST be finite.

req-spatialref-document-2.text: asref:pixelRegistration states where a cell's value is located within the cell (PixelCenter: a point sample at the center; PixelCorner: a value for the cell's area); a description MUST NOT use it to shift the affine, whose coefficients are corner-based under both registrations.

req-spatialref-document-3.text: A singular transform MAY be represented; a consumer that evaluates the inverse SHOULD fail when the determinant is zero, as hxf:column and hxf:row do, rather than return a cell.

req-spatialref-document-4.text: Floating implementations MUST document conditioning and tolerance policies; exact nonzero determinants alone do not establish numerical stability.

req-spatialref-document-5.text: Each GCP MUST include both image and ground coordinate pairs; elevation is optional.
req-spatialref-document-5.context: Ground-control-point coordinates MAY use a different CRS from an affine transform.

req-spatialref-document-6.context: A CubicRationalTransform holds four finite 20-coefficient vectors and five offset/scale pairs.

req-spatialref-document-7.text: A polynomialBasis IRI MUST identify a published contract defining all 20 ordered monomials, normalization, input CRS/units and pixel convention.

req-spatialref-document-8.text: Different coefficient orders MUST NOT be interchanged.
req-spatialref-document-8.context: A polynomialBasis IRI MUST identify a published contract defining all 20 ordered monomials, normalization, input CRS/units and pixel convention.

req-spatialref-document-9.text: A profile MUST identify the complete contract, not merely label a model “RPC”.

req-spatialref-document-10.text: A consumer that evaluates rational polynomial transforms SHOULD report a basis it does not support, and SHOULD NOT evaluate it under another basis; this working draft mandates no RPC execution engine, and no conformance class of the Processing Model evaluates one.

req-spatialref-document-11.text: Such a consumer SHOULD raise an explicit evaluation error for a zero denominator.
req-spatialref-document-11.context: For a known basis, normalize each input q = (coordinate − offset) / scale, evaluate each numerator and denominator in the declared monomial order, then recover each output as output = offset + scale × numerator / denominator.

req-spatialref-document-12.text: No conformance class of the Processing Model evaluates the transform; a consumer that does, as the hxf function library does, SHOULD take the column and row of a world point as the floors of its inverse-affine grid coordinates whatever the registration.
